mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real GDP and housing starts by more than 2% within 3 months signals a robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST increase > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between GDPC1, HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls and a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within 2 months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between PAYEMS increases, UNRATE decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the consumer price index signals inflationary pressures, which erodes real earnings and increases the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 5% within 2 months signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
